about: Every text the Kotlin backend's Lua engine REFUSES, and why each one is a
refusal rather than a gap.
`LuaScriptEngine` offers the author's ECMAScript to `sce-build`'s frontend,
and what the frontend will not lower is refused — W3C SCXML §scxml-5.9.1,
the processor places `error.execution` on the internal queue. Until
2026-08-30 it was handed to `EcmaScriptToLuaTransformer` instead and
guessed at; that unit is retired and this file is what replaced the number
measuring the distance to its retirement.
WHY A LIST AND NOT A COUNT. The count it replaced was a ceiling over the
fallback's uses, driven down to zero. A ceiling cannot work here for two
separate reasons and both are worth stating. First, `rewriter=0` became
STRUCTURAL the day the unit was deleted — nothing in this tree can move
that number, and a predicate nothing can move is not a measurement.
Second, a refusal is not by itself a defect: a suite that asks for `foo`
with nothing named `foo` gets exactly what the clause requires, so `how
many` cannot separate the specification working from a shape the frontend
should learn. WHICH ONES can.
HELD IN BOTH DIRECTIONS by `scripts/gates/w3c-kotlin.sh`, which reads the
census the engine writes. A refused text with no entry here is RED — an
unclassified refusal is a gap nobody looked at. An entry no run produces is
RED too: a list that keeps a case it no longer describes cannot be trusted
in the other direction either.
THE LIST GOES DOWN. Each entry is one of three things, and its `why` says
which: a shape the frontend should learn (the entry leaves when it does), a
caller handing Lua through the ECMAScript door (the entry leaves when the
caller re-tags), or the specification's own refusal (the entry stays, and
cites the clause). Adding an entry of either of the first two kinds is a
claim to argue in `docs/SCE_LUA_TRANSLATION_SEAM.md`, not a way to make
this lane green.
`text` is the AUTHOR'S spelling — `ScriptSource.source`, the text the
document wrote — and not the lowering, because a refusal has no lowering.

why: `never_declared` is a name the session's scope has never been told
about, so the frontend refuses the expression and the engine reports
it. That is what the clause asks for — an expression the datamodel
cannot evaluate places `error.execution` on the internal queue — and
it is what `DatamodelReadJsonTest` asks the engine for on purpose:
the reader must answer null for a `<data>` that is not there rather
than invent a value for it.
THIS ENTRY DOES NOT LEAVE. It is the one kind of refusal that is not
a gap: no shape the frontend could learn would make an undeclared
name resolvable, because resolving it is exactly what the clause
forbids.
A Lua table constructor with a bracketed key, handed through the
ECMAScript door ON PURPOSE. It is the control half of
`ScriptLanguageSeamTest.theLoweredScriptArmSkipsTheRunTimeLoweringToo`:
the same characters tagged `lua` must reach the interpreter as
written, and the same characters tagged `ecmascript` must NOT, or the
tag changed nothing and the case measures one path twice.
⚠ What the control observes NARROWED when
`EcmaScriptToLuaTransformer` was retired, and it got stronger. The
rewriter used to mangle this text into something that ran and left no
readable `o.k`; the frontend refuses it, which the same assertion
reads as the same 'not 7'. A wrong answer and a refusal are both 'the
tag was not ignored', and only the refusal is what the clause wants.
THIS ENTRY DOES NOT LEAVE EITHER, for as long as that case does: it
is a deliberate mis-tag, not a shape the frontend should learn. A
frontend that accepted it would be parsing Lua as ECMAScript.
